dialogues.speaker: Ovsyannikov
dialogues.text: We're talking about how every single tavern in Snezhnograd is diluting proper fire-water with fruit juice these days!

dialogues.speaker: Ovsyannikov
dialogues.text: How ridiculous is that? There used to be a proper way to drink fire-water: you gulp it down in one go, then you chase it with a slice of pickle and a piece of black bread. That's the right way to do it.

dialogues.speaker: Ovsyannikov
dialogues.text: That's exactly how my elders did it when they were out on the Belyi Tsar's campaigns!

dialogues.speaker: Ovsyannikov
dialogues.text: And look at what we're stuck with now. We've completely lost the old ways, I'm telling you. Everything is just frills and gimmicks these days.

dialogues.speaker: Lyubimova
dialogues.text: "Project Stuzha" my foot! Someone must have offended the black god again or something...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who is this "black god" you're talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Lyubimova
dialogues.text: You younger generation wouldn't know a thing about it. This "black god" is a terribly wicked fiend, a real monster, and it was because of its curse that the old Tsar bit the dust back in the day...

dialogues.speaker: Lyubimova
dialogues.text: Lately, Snezhnograd has been in a terribly wild uproar, a real madhouse, and I say it's because that "black god" is coming back again!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That sounds a little farfetched, to be honest...

dialogues.speaker: Lyubimova
dialogues.text: Not at all! You've heard of Northland Bank, but do you honestly believe it's just a place for coin? I'm telling you, that bank wasn't even a thing when the old Tsar was still around!

dialogues.speaker: Lyubimova
dialogues.text: That bank exists because the "black god" had marked every Mora in existence. The Tsaritsa ordered it established to give them a terribly strict washing, a real cleaning, before they came back out.

dialogues.speaker: Lyubimova
dialogues.text: You'd better believe it! I heard this from a personal attendant of the Tsaritsa's, so it must be true.

dialogues.speaker: Lyubimova
dialogues.text: Isn't that so? So, we must all be careful, and keep from heading out of doors if we can.

dialogues.speaker: Lyubimova
dialogues.text: But if we must leave the house, stop every three steps. Just stand still for a moment. That is the only way to avoid bumping into the unclean.
